content.comment_body: Hello, I am using a [product_name] PLC with article number [article_no] and firmware [version_no]. I'm encountering issues when trying to load a program to the [product_name], even though the connection between my PC and the device is established. A week ago, I used a similar device with the same article number but a different firmware ([version_no]), and I was able to download the program without any problems. What could be causing this issue and how can it be fixed? I appreciate any assistance, thank you.
Could you share your project file? That way, I can help check it with the [product_name] PLC.
Which version of the [product_name] programming software are you using?
Hi [user_name], please take a look at the attached photo. Thanks.
Hi [user_name], I tried using a very simple program with just an input connected to a coil, but still couldn't download any program, regardless of its complexity.
I requested the project file to examine the [product_name] settings and configuration, not specifically the logic.

Hello [user_name], your software version is [version_no]. This version does not support a [product_name] PLC with firmware [version_no] (FS05). Instead, it supports models with firmware FS01 to FS03. To program models with newer firmware, you need to update your software to at least [version_no] or higher. You can obtain this upgrade for free and download it from [url]. Once downloaded, make sure to use the correct installer for your Windows version (32bit or 64bit). Run the setup as administrator and follow the installation instructions.

Hello [user_name], The original poster mentioned using a [product_name] PLC with article number [article_no] and firmware [version_no] and facing issues loading the program, while the higher firmware version worked fine. Let me know if that's accurate. Thanks.

Hello [user_name], There might be some misunderstanding regarding the situation, maybe due to how the topic was expressed. Based on the provided photos, the software version appears to be incorrect for the model in question. The topic starter should clarify further.

After researching some previous discussions from November 2016, I found an issue related to [product_name] programming software [version_no]. In my old forum post, I suspected a bug where projects created with [version_no] may cause problems if opened and modified with [version_no], especially when changing hardware in the source file. For example, selecting hardware [article_no] caused an 'Error loading the panel' message. Acknowledging the error led to varying outcomes, depending on the program. Opening the program in another older version exposed the error, and multiple changes were made. While both the simulation and the real [product_name] model worked without errors, it was not possible to select the specific hardware. See attached videos.

Hello [user_name], Sorry for the delayed response, I was on vacation. I double-checked the information I provided earlier and can confirm that I am facing the issue with the lower firmware version. I will try updating my software to [version_no] and let you know the result.
Dear [user_name], I was able to download the program successfully after updating to [version_no]. Thank you very much for your support.
Hi [user_name], glad to hear you managed to download the program. You can rate [user_name] for his assistance, it really helps and encourages further helpful contributions for others in need. Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The main user experience challenge is the incompatibility between different versions of [product_name] programming software and firmware revisions of the hardware. Users are confused about which software versions support which devices, leading to errors and failed program transfers. Ambiguity also arises from various hardware and firmware variations, and system error messages do not clearly explain the underlying causes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the programming software to seamlessly support all hardware revisions without needing to manage version compatibility. Clear, actionable error messages are anticipated to indicate when a mismatch between software and firmware prevents program loading.
